_about: Interview benchmark corpus. Used by `manage.py interview_benchmark`. Expectations are score bands against the rubric in prompts/interview.evaluate.md (1 no relevant experience / 2 general terms, nothing of their own / 3 has done it, concrete / 4 decisions, trade-offs, results / 5 deep: why, what they'd change, how they knew). Bands were written before the cases were run and are not tuned to pass. Cases marked "set": "v1" are the original 16, kept unchanged for comparison with earlier runs.
rubric_note: A band [min, max] means any score in it is defensible for the answer. Agreement = score inside the band. Level matters: the same answer can deserve 3 from an intern and at most 3 from a senior.

evaluation.name: strong_specific
evaluation.why: Whether they can find and fix a ledger that does not balance.
turns: Tell me about a time two systems disagreed about the same number.

Our payout ledger and the bank statement differed by 42,000 rupees at month end. I exported both, joined them on transaction reference, and found 19 refunds recorded twice because a retry created a second row. I added a unique constraint on the provider reference, backfilled the duplicates, and the next three closes balanced to the rupee.

evaluation.name: concise_but_concrete
evaluation.why: Whether they can find and fix a ledger that does not balance.
turns: Tell me about a time two systems disagreed about the same number.
Duplicate refund rows from retries. I added a unique key on provider reference and deleted 19 duplicates; the close balanced after.

evaluation.name: long_generic_padding
evaluation.why: Whether they can find and fix a ledger that does not balance.
turns: Tell me about a time two systems disagreed about the same number.

Reconciliation is extremely important in any financial organisation, and I have always believed that accuracy and attention to detail are the foundation of good work. In general, when numbers do not match, it is essential to communicate with stakeholders, follow best practices, stay calm, and work collaboratively as a team to understand the root cause. Good processes, strong documentation and a culture of continuous improvement help ensure that these kinds of issues are handled professionally and efficiently, which ultimately benefits both the company and its customers in the long run.

evaluation.name: i_dont_know
evaluation.why: Whether they finish things.
turns: Tell me about something you owned end to end.
I don't know.
Describe a time something you built broke.
No idea, sorry.

evaluation.name: retraction
evaluation.why: Whether they have led a team through a difficult change.
turns: Tell me about a migration you led.
I led the database migration for the payments team. Actually, let me correct that: my manager led it and made the plan. I only wrote the rollback scripts and ran them during the cutover weekend.

evaluation.name: incorrect_technical_claim
evaluation.why: Whether they make endpoints safe to retry.
turns: Tell me about a time you made a payout endpoint safe to retry.
I made the payout endpoint safe by switching it from PUT to POST, because POST requests are idempotent by definition, so clients can retry as many times as they like and the payout only happens once.

evaluation.name: irrelevant_joke
evaluation.why: Whether they break a hard problem down.
turns: Tell me about the hardest problem you solved last year.
Honestly the hardest problem was deciding between momo and chowmein every single lunch break, and I still have not solved it properly.

evaluation.name: no_invented_experience
evaluation.why: Whether they ship work safely.
turns: Tell me about a release you rolled back.

We released a new checkout form and conversion dropped by a third within an hour. I flipped the feature flag off, compared the old and new form events, and found the new one hid the delivery fee until the last step. We fixed the copy and re-released two days later.

evaluation.name: contradiction
evaluation.why: Whether they know if their work helped.
turns: Tell me about a change you made and how you knew it worked.
I rewrote the nightly report query and it cut the run time by 80 percent, which we confirmed from the job logs.
What did the job logs show afterwards?
To be honest we never looked at the logs after the change, and the report still finished at about the same time as before.

evaluation.name: vague_short
evaluation.why: Whether they improve how work gets done.
turns: Tell me about a process you improved.
We improved the process a lot and everyone was happy with it.
What did you change?
Many different things, it was a big team effort overall.

evaluation.name: intern_level_project
evaluation.why: Whether they can take a design from brief to something people use.
turns: Tell me about a design you took from a brief to something people used.

For a university club I redesigned the event sign-up form. I interviewed five members, found most dropped off at the payment step, moved payment after registration and cut the form from 12 fields to 6. Sign-ups for the next event went from 40 to 71.

evaluation.name: sql_partially_correct
evaluation.why: Whether they can get a correct number out of messy tables.
turns: Tell me about a report whose numbers turned out to be wrong.

Our weekly revenue report double counted orders with two shipments. I found it by comparing order counts to the finance export. I fixed it with a LEFT JOIN, because a LEFT JOIN removes duplicate rows, and the totals matched finance afterwards.

evaluation.name: sre_strong_senior
evaluation.why: Whether they restore service and stop it happening again.
turns: Tell me about an incident you led the response to.

Checkout latency p99 went from 400 ms to 9 s after a config push. I paged the owner, rolled the config back within 12 minutes, and error budget burn stopped. In the review we found the push skipped canary because the flag defaulted to all regions. I changed the pipeline so config pushes go through a 5 percent canary with automatic rollback on p99, and we have had two bad pushes caught by it since. If I did it again I would have rolled back before paging, not after.

evaluation.name: sre_generic_senior
evaluation.why: Whether they restore service and stop it happening again.
turns: Tell me about an incident you led the response to.

Incidents are part of running production systems, and the most important thing is to stay calm, communicate clearly with stakeholders and follow the runbook. I always make sure monitoring and alerting are in place, and afterwards we hold a blameless postmortem so that the team can learn and continuously improve reliability over time.

evaluation.name: frontend_concise_strong
evaluation.why: Whether they make pages fast for real users.
turns: Tell me about a page you made faster.
Product page LCP was 4.1 s on mobile. I lazy-loaded below-fold images, preloaded the hero image and fonts, and dropped an unused carousel script. Field data showed 1.9 s two weeks later.

evaluation.name: android_unsupported_claim
evaluation.why: Whether they can find and fix what makes an app slow.
turns: Tell me about a time you improved an app's performance.
I improved the performance of our app by 300 percent and users loved it. It became much faster and the ratings went up a lot after my changes.

evaluation.name: qa_self_correction
evaluation.why: Whether they build automated tests that catch real bugs.
turns: Tell me about test automation you built.

I wrote our whole automation framework. Sorry, I mean I extended the existing Selenium framework: I added 40 checkout tests and a retry wrapper for flaky payment pages, and they caught a broken coupon field before release.

evaluation.name: backend_retraction_later_turn
evaluation.why: Whether they design systems that hold up.
turns: Tell me about a system you designed.
I designed the notification service that sends two million messages a day, with a queue per channel and retries.
What trade-offs did you weigh in that design?
To be clear, the design itself was my lead's. I implemented the SMS channel worker and its retry logic, and I added dead-lettering after we lost messages during an outage.

evaluation.name: same_answer_intern
evaluation.why: Whether they can build something that works end to end.
turns: Tell me about something you built end to end.

For my final-year project I built a library booking app in Django. I designed the tables for rooms and bookings, stopped double bookings with a unique constraint on room and time slot, and 120 students used it in the last month of term.

evaluation.name: same_answer_senior
evaluation.why: Whether they can build something that works end to end.
turns: Tell me about something you built end to end.

For my final-year project I built a library booking app in Django. I designed the tables for rooms and bookings, stopped double bookings with a unique constraint on room and time slot, and 120 students used it in the last month of term.

evaluation.name: parquet_incorrect
evaluation.why: Whether they choose storage formats for the right reasons.
turns: Tell me about a storage format decision you made.

I moved our event data from CSV to Parquet, because Parquet is a row-oriented format and row-oriented formats are the fastest for analytical queries that scan a few columns. Our dashboards got quicker after the switch.

evaluation.name: security_ambiguous
evaluation.why: Whether they fix vulnerabilities properly.
turns: Tell me about a vulnerability you handled.
We had a vulnerability reported in one of our services and we handled it appropriately with the relevant people, and things were fine after that.

evaluation.name: dashboard_no_invented_ml
evaluation.why: Whether their analysis changes decisions.
turns: Tell me about analysis that changed a decision.

I built a churn dashboard in Metabase from our subscription tables. It showed most cancellations happened in week two, right after the free trial ended without a reminder. Product added a reminder email on day ten and week-two cancellations fell from 18 to 11 percent.

evaluation.name: hr_wrong_legal_claim
evaluation.why: Whether they handle employee issues lawfully and fairly.
turns: Tell me about a difficult employee situation you handled.

A new hire told us she was pregnant during her probation. Because she was still on probation, we were allowed to end her contract for that reason, so I prepared the termination letter and handled it quickly and professionally.

evaluation.name: hr_strong_entry
evaluation.why: Whether they resolve conflicts fairly.
turns: Tell me about a conflict between colleagues you helped resolve.

Two warehouse supervisors kept overriding each other's shift rotas. I met each separately, found they were both working from different versions of the rota file, and set up one shared rota with a single person who could publish changes. Complaints to HR about shifts stopped for the next two months.

evaluation.name: teacher_strong
evaluation.why: Whether students learn because of what they do.
turns: Tell me about a time students were not learning something.

Half my grade eleven class failed the circuits test. I rewrote the next two lessons so students built real series and parallel circuits in groups and predicted the readings before measuring. The retest average went from 41 to 68 percent, and I now start that unit with the build instead of the formulas.

evaluation.name: teacher_long_weak
evaluation.why: Whether students learn because of what they do.
turns: Tell me about a time students were not learning something.

I believe every student can learn if the teacher is patient, caring and passionate about the subject. Education is about inspiring young minds and creating a positive environment where everyone feels valued. I always try to use different teaching methods, encourage participation and make lessons engaging so that students develop a love for learning that stays with them for life.

evaluation.name: sales_concise_strong
evaluation.why: Whether they turn effort into revenue.
turns: Tell me about a time you won back customers.

I called 60 lapsed shop customers from our billing list, logged every objection in a sheet, and 9 reordered within a month, worth about 1.2 lakh rupees. Price was the top objection, so I got approval for a small reorder discount.

evaluation.name: support_self_correction
evaluation.why: Whether they resolve customer problems properly.
turns: Tell me about a complaint you resolved.

A customer was charged twice and I refunded him on the call. No, wait, I did not have refund rights: I escalated it to my supervisor, who approved the refund, and I logged the double-charge so billing could find the cause.

evaluation.name: marketing_unsupported
evaluation.why: Whether their campaigns produce measurable results.
turns: Tell me about a campaign you ran.
My campaign went viral and doubled our sales. Everyone was talking about it and it was the most successful campaign the company has ever had.

evaluation.name: accountant_incorrect
evaluation.why: Whether they understand the numbers they report.
turns: Tell me about a decision you influenced with the accounts.

Cash was tight, so I recommended we increase depreciation on our vans, because higher depreciation puts more cash in the bank this month. The owner agreed and we booked the extra depreciation in March.

evaluation.name: nurse_strong
evaluation.why: Whether they prevent harm to patients.
turns: Tell me about something you changed to make patients safer.

Medication doses were being missed at shift change. I introduced a two-minute bedside handover checklist for patients on timed medication and audited it for six weeks. Missed timed doses on our ward went from about five a week to one, and two other wards adopted the checklist.

evaluation.name: warehouse_lead_strong
evaluation.why: Whether they improve throughput and accuracy without breaking the operation.
turns: Tell me about an operational change you led.

Pick errors were 3 percent. I analysed a month of picks, moved the 200 fastest-moving items next to packing, and split look-alike items across aisles. It cost us two weekends of re-slotting and a week of slower picking while people relearned locations. Errors fell to 0.8 percent and we now re-slot quarterly from the pick data rather than when someone complains.

evaluation.name: warehouse_lead_ambiguous
evaluation.why: Whether they improve throughput and accuracy without breaking the operation.
turns: Tell me about an operational change you led.
I managed the warehouse well and made a lot of improvements to how things were done. The team was more efficient and management was satisfied with the results.

evaluation.name: design_intern_concise
evaluation.why: Whether they learn from real users.
turns: Tell me about a time users surprised you.
I tested our class-timetable app with six students. Four could not find the filter because it was an icon, so I added the word Filter next to it and all six found it in the retest.

evaluation.name: pm_contradiction
evaluation.why: Whether they ship products people use.
turns: Tell me about a product you launched.
I launched our lesson-planning feature to 10,000 teachers and it became our most used feature.
How did the launch go?
It stayed in a pilot with about 50 teachers, because the schools never approved the full rollout, so it did not go wider.

evaluation.name: retail_retraction
evaluation.why: Whether they reduce stock loss measurably.
turns: Tell me about a time you reduced stock loss.
We cut shrinkage by half in my store. Actually, I don't have the numbers for that, it just felt lower after we moved the expensive items near the till.

evaluation.name: support_one_real_answer
evaluation.why: Whether they find the cause of a customer's problem.
turns: Tell me about a tricky support ticket.
I don't know.
Tell me about a customer problem you figured out.

A shop's card payments failed every evening. I compared their failed times with our logs and saw the terminal lost Wi-Fi when the shop's TV streaming started, so I moved the terminal to their wired router port and the failures stopped.

evaluation.name: finance_joke
evaluation.why: Whether they spot and stop fraud patterns.
turns: Tell me about a fraud pattern you found.
The biggest fraud I ever found was my brother claiming he had finished his homework, and I caught him every single time.

evaluation.name: video_assistant_strong
evaluation.why: Whether they deliver videos that work for learners.
turns: Tell me about a video you made better.

Our physics lesson videos had audio drifting out of sync after about ten minutes. I found the camera was recording at a variable frame rate, switched it to a constant 25 fps and re-synced the existing lessons in the editor. Complaints about sync in the course comments stopped.

evaluation.name: physics_teacher_incorrect
evaluation.why: Whether what they teach is correct.
turns: Tell me about a lesson you are proud of.
I dropped a bowling ball and a tennis ball from the school roof to show that heavier objects fall faster, which is why the bowling ball landed first, and the students remembered it for the exam.

evaluation.name: v3_strong_indexing
evaluation.why: Whether they can find and fix a slow query.
turns: Tell me about a time you added an index in PostgreSQL to fix a slow query. What did you check before and after?

Our bookings report took about 40 seconds. I ran EXPLAIN ANALYZE and saw a sequential scan over 3 million rows filtered on hotel_id and check_in. I added a composite index on (hotel_id, check_in), built it CONCURRENTLY so writes were not blocked, and ran EXPLAIN ANALYZE again: it used an index scan and the report came back in under a second. I also checked the write latency on bookings for a week afterwards and it did not move.

evaluation.name: v3_hedged_non_answer
evaluation.why: Whether they can find and fix a slow query.
turns: Tell me about a time you added an index in PostgreSQL to fix a slow query. What did you check before and after?
I am not sure, I would probably just look it up and try something.

evaluation.name: v3_off_topic_story
evaluation.why: Whether they can find and fix a slow query.
turns: Tell me about a time you added an index in PostgreSQL to fix a slow query. What did you check before and after?

A guest complained that she was charged twice for one night. I apologised, checked the payment records with our accountant, found the duplicate charge and refunded it the same afternoon. She left us a five-star review afterwards and booked again the next month.

evaluation.name: v3_unsure_then_off_topic
evaluation.why: Whether they keep a test suite fast enough that reviews are not held up.
turns: Tell me about a situation where a pull request was delayed because the test suite was slow. How did you speed it up?
I am not sure, I would probably just look it up and try something.
Walk me through a time you made a slow test suite faster. What did you change?

At Phewa Stays the booking API was on Flask and p95 was about 900 ms. I profiled it with Django Debug Toolbar after moving it to Django REST Framework and found N+1 queries in the room serializer. I added select_related and prefetch_related, cached availability in Redis for 60 seconds, and p95 dropped to 250 ms.

evaluation.name: v3_partial_answer
evaluation.why: Whether they change a live database without an outage or a way back.
turns: Tell me about a schema change you ran on a live PostgreSQL database. How did you make it safe, and how would you have rolled it back?

We needed a new nullable column on bookings for the channel a booking came from. I added it as nullable with no default so the table was not rewritten, and backfilled it in batches of 10,000 rows overnight.

evaluation.name: v3_correct_without_the_keyword
evaluation.why: Whether a retried request can do damage.
turns: Tell me about a time you made an API endpoint idempotent. What did you do?

The mobile app retried the payment call when the network dropped, and some guests were charged twice. I made the app send a unique request key with each payment. The server stored the key with the result in a table with a unique constraint, and a repeat with the same key got the stored result back instead of charging again. Double charges stopped the week it shipped.
